picks.headline: AI trained to 'think' like human pathologists may be better at spotting cancer
picks.excerpt: Pathology-o3 was trained on pathologists' actual search behavior — how they pan and zoom across a slide — rather than on pre-cropped regions. It flagged 100% of cancer-positive slides in testing, with a deliberately tolerated 15.5% false-positive rate.
picks.rationale: Freshest pick and the most method-shifting: training on human search behavior instead of curated crops, with a hard sensitivity/false-positive tradeoff stated up front.

picks.headline: Specificity-driven protein binder design with Odin-Multi
picks.excerpt: A Technical University of Denmark team optimizes one binder sequence against many target complexes at once, applying attractive objectives to on-targets and repulsive ones to off-targets. The premise: a useful binder is defined as much by what it does not bind.
picks.rationale: Primary-source protein design work that reframes the objective — negative design against off-targets — a concrete recipe other binder-design pipelines can copy.

picks.headline: AI Behavior Impacted by Internal Confidence Levels
picks.excerpt: Google DeepMind researchers report in Nature Machine Intelligence that LLMs use internal confidence signals to decide when to abstain from answering — a form of metacognitive control paralleling humans and animals. It reframes hallucination as a calibration problem, not just a knowledge gap.
picks.rationale: Cognition slot with immediate practical bite: if abstention rides on internal confidence, hallucination becomes a calibration target rather than a knowledge hole.

picks.headline: JWST Ruled Out Finding Tiny Moons Around An Exoplanet - That's Great News
picks.excerpt: A JWST non-detection of exomoons sets a useful upper limit, and the authors argue machine-learning analysis of repeated observations is the path to pulling real exomoon signals out of instrumental noise. It is a template for how ML changes null results into constraints.
picks.rationale: Astronomy slot, and the rare story about a null result becoming a measurement — ML as the instrument that turns 'we saw nothing' into a bound.

picks.headline: Researchers eye AI revolution in natural disaster forecasts
picks.excerpt: Swiss researchers are pairing roughly 100 petabytes of NASA Earth-observation and climate data with supercomputing to train AI models that cut forecast turnaround to minutes. The goal is spotting precursors of floods and glacier collapses that physics-based models miss.
picks.rationale: Earth-science slot with hard numbers — 100 PB of NASA data, forecast turnaround down to minutes — and a stated aim of catching precursors physics models miss.
